0.content:
Sandrone, the Seventh Harbinger and Alain Guillotin's automaton, is Columbina's best friend, though Sandrone would never say so. Columbina first followed her around trying to work out how the wind-up key on her back moved, until Sandrone whirled round and offered to put a key on her too; Columbina wore one for a few days and has "looked out for her even more since then". At a restaurant, when Columbina froze before a frightened clerk holding the bill, Sandrone filled in the reimbursement slip, put her on Sandrone's tab and asked, "Isn't this just who you are?" No "you should be", no "you could do better": that acceptance made her happy. Sandrone publicly calls her a nuisance with "zero social graces".

Sandrone banned her daytime singing (it unnerved others and broke Sandrone's sleep), so Columbina sang outside her door at night and was chased off. Columbina once joked that Sandrone should drink oil instead of coffee and got cursed out for it. Whenever Sandrone was angry with her, Sandrone gave her presents. In Nod-Krai Sandrone was technically obliged to bring her in under the Palestar Edict but had no interest in doing so. She rebuked Columbina for spoiling her fight with Rerir, then agreed to summon Arlecchino for her for old tea parties' sake.

In 6.3 Sandrone computed the world-formula that guided Columbina home and hid the real formula in Pulonia, leaving a false one in herself to fool Dottore. It cost her: afterward her key stopped, and even trilunar power could not wake her. In the 6.7 Fontinalia she returned. She had planned to make Columbina "jump for once", but Columbina sensed her, teleported her over, and was hugged; the reunion was caught on Kamera for the film. Columbina asked to visit Alain Guillotin's grave with her, and there told Alain that Sandrone is brilliant, has made friends and takes care of them. She also revealed that Sandrone likes bitter coffee, piano music and hugs, to Sandrone's horror. Sandrone's key now sometimes turns faster; it turned faster when Columbina told her she admired her. By 7.0 Sandrone was back in Snezhnograd.

1.comment: Columbina: Silvermoon Hall and the kuuhenki
1.content:
Silvermoon Hall is a cavern on Hiisi Island where Columbina hid after leaving the Fatui: a field of blue flowers, pools of water, and a rocking chair for moongazing. A great boulder once sealed it from the Scions and the Fatui; after 6.3 she rolled it aside, because hiding no longer seemed necessary and her friends had invited her into their homes. Kuuhenki, the small moon spirits of Nod-Krai, live with her. She tells them stories, sings them to sleep, has snowball fights with them and prefers their company because they never hide their thoughts.

In the reputation quests (Silvermoon Hall: Selenic Chronicles, 6.0 onward) she shares memories of the Fatui, helps the kuuhenki painter Maalaus, takes a kuuhenki's lyre to the mechanic Aino, guides a lost Scion child home and learns the Scions' new motto, "May the moonlight connect us". After 6.3 she revives Luonnotar, opens her eyes to see her new winged statue, takes Maalaus to paint on the moon, and starts cooking and leaving gifts for friends.

2.comment: Columbina: Lauma and the Frostmoon Scions
2.content:
The Frostmoon Scions of Hiisi Island, descendants of Hyperborea, awaited a prophesied new Moon Goddess. When Kuutar was born they worshipped her, carved Statues of the New Moon in her image and asked for more than she could give, until she left. Generations later Lauma, the current Moonchanter, met her, apologised for her ancestors' greed, and asked her to stay hidden for both their sakes, a request Lauma herself calls a little rude. Lauma dreams that the moon and her believers can one day share a toast. After 6.3 Columbina took her advice and came to live among the Scions.

Columbina had never seen antlers as splendid as Lauma's. She secretly visits Lauma's home and hums her lullaby to soothe the painful moon-tides that afflict Lauma. She teases her too: aim a moonbeam at Lauma's head and her antlers grow tall enough to spear high fruit ("You get scolded"). Lauma hid Columbina, searched the Hyperborean ruins for her name, and hugged her breathless when she returned. Columbina gave Lauma the Eternal Moon Marrow.

The older Scions still bow and keep their distance; the children are curious. Columbina rehearsed answering Scion questions with the Traveler and wants to invite artists to record the Scions' happy lives. The Scions gave her statue wings, and she opened her eyes to admire it before Lauma's feast. A Scion elder once told Lauma the Moon Goddess had not answered her prayers in a hundred and two years. Lauma could not bring herself to say that the goddess was a lonely "person" too.

3.content:
Roughly a century after her birth, Kuutar left the Scions and accepted the Tsaritsa's offer of a "second home". She was made the Third of the Eleven Fatui Harbingers under the names Columbina and The Damselette. She was never sent to seize a Gnosis or anything else; the Tsaritsa sought only a Moon Goddess's power. She asked repeatedly when her task would begin and was told "the time has not yet come", so she walked, watched the moon and sang. Tartaglia never understood why "that girl" ranked third and felt something was off about her. The Wanderer called her oblivious and unfeeling. Arlecchino called her a very special Harbinger whose answers are always interesting.

In Nod-Krai the Tsaritsa finally called in the task, which consumed much of her divine power. She told her unit she had finished what Her Majesty asked and wished to see to personal matters, and left; her subordinates went to Dottore. The Palestar Edict, the Tsaritsa's highest command, ordered her retrieval at any cost, but her old friends had no interest in enforcing it. Dottore used it as cover to seize her power, and once that came to light the Tsaritsa revoked it (6.3). She remembers the perks of rank fondly: free trains and free Korolevskiy Troupe tickets.

4.content:
Dottore was the first Harbinger to approach her, politely asking for help with kuuvahki and Light Realm research. She liked being offered a choice and enjoyed his early praise. Then the praise became "Not quite enough" and "You're capable of more", and she realised he saw only the power she ought to reach. He called her a sister and meant it: "What's a little discomfort among family? We endure for each other, surely." It reminded her of the Scions' eyes beneath the altar, so she stopped helping him. At Signora's funeral she innocently asked after "the Segment in the prime of his life".

In Nod-Krai he revived Rerir and timed it to her weakness. On Moon-Prayer Night (6.2) he hijacked her return to the moon with a false moon built from Hyperborean knowledge, froze time and stole the Moon Marrows. To deny him the Three Moons' power she threw herself into a moon gate. As the Trilune Goddess (6.3) she returned, fought him with the Traveler, Flins, Lauma and Nefer, and vaporized him with a beam of lunar energy that shattered his artificial Marrow. She now refuses to remake the world at will, because that would make her no different from him. His final end came later in Sumeru (6.6), without her.

5.content:
For centuries Columbina did not recognise herself in any of her names (Kuutar, The Damselette, Goddess) and told the Traveler to pick "whichever takes your fancy". After Rerir's expulsion her strength failed and Teyvat's rejection began to erase her. Alice and Nicole explained that she had no anchor in the world, no name she had chosen. She drifted unseen through Nasha Town and the Frostmoon Enclave and could not follow her friends into the Hyperborean ruins. Nicole realised a name need not come from the past; the Traveler went to Silvermoon Hall and called "Columbina", and she returned whole. She named herself Columbina Hyposelenia, "born beneath the moon", and by extension "born beneath this world".

She says the name turned from a Fatui codename into "something my friends call me". She later reflected that she had thought a name was only an alias, but now sees it as what connects her to the world and its people, their friendship and support made visible. Arlecchino had suggested beforehand that she change her name once Rerir was dealt with, and called the result "A fine name."

6.content:
Arlecchino used to appear silently behind her to "test" her. Columbina tried the game back and failed until she used kuuvahki, which gave the Knave such a fright that she never played again. Columbina knows Arlecchino descends from the Crimson Moon Dynasty. Hearing the House of the Hearth children call Arlecchino "Father", she assumed it was a rule and did the same, and learned how quiet the House could get. In 6.1 Arlecchino answered Sandrone's summons and came to Nod-Krai 'solely in a personal capacity', not on Fatui business. She burned away the Wild Hunt cornering Columbina at Thunderclap Reef and opened a path into the Crimson Moon subspace for the Iridescent Moon Marrow. She held the exit open at the cost of Abyss-corrupted hands. The Marrow restored Columbina to her Harbinger-era strength, and she gave it to Arlecchino.

After Dottore's ambush Arlecchino declared that if the Tsaritsa did not lift the ban on Harbingers fighting one another, she would fight Dottore herself as Peruere; she later helped pull the Frost Moon into Teyvat. After 6.3, grieving Sandrone, Columbina still comforted Arlecchino, who credited the Traveler's friendship with the change in her. Columbina would side with Arlecchino against the Doctor in any meeting.

7.comment: Columbina: Moon's Reflection and the Three Moon Sisters
7.content:
The Moon's Reflection is a space where time runs backwards; Columbina believed Rerir and his fiancée Tholindis had died on entering it (Tholindis leapt in long ago hoping to change the past, and her soul still wandered there). Columbina survived and walked deeper into the past. There Sonnet, goddess of the Iridescent Moon, found her and brought her to Canon (Frost Moon) and Aria (Eternal Moon), imprisoned by Nibelung since the war of funerary flame. She told them of the future: offerings, opera houses, a friend with a clockwork key, a former angel, and Moon-Prayer Night with water-ball games, face stickers and shared candy. The goddesses were moved and a little envious ("Wow..."). Her plan was to "die" in the prison, scatter her body as moonlight over ancient Nod-Krai and be reassembled in the future. They gave her their authorities; becoming mortal, they asked to be sent home to face the end together.

Canon asked why her eyes were always closed. She warned that shutting out lies had also shut out the truth, and made Columbina swear to open them and see her friends' true smiles. None of the sisters recognised her lullaby, and they had never heard of kuuvahki. Columbina later understood that her sisters wanted to protect rather than rule, and felt she had inherited a "family tendency". In the present, Sandrone's world-formula and the Frost Moon being pulled through the false sky reunited her body (Nod-Krai's moonlight) and spirit (held in Luonnotar) with the trilunar authority.

8.comment: Columbina: Rerir and the Wild Hunt
8.content:
Columbina told the Traveler their Wild Hunt foe was the "Rächer of Solnari", a title she had heard among the Fatui, which they recognised as Rerir, one of the Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah. At Starsand Shoal she teleported the Traveler, Paimon, Flins, Sandrone and Pulonia out of his reach. In 6.1 he attacked her on Hiisi Island and overpowered everyone; she took a scrape pushing Jahoda clear and teleported the group away. With all three Moon Marrows and Albedo and Durin's array siphoning his power into her, she overpowered him and flicked him through a moon gate held by Dainsleif, out of Teyvat.

In the Moon's Reflection she met a sane, remorseful Rerir. He said Dottore had revived him and that he had stopped running after recognising Dainsleif. He cleared her path and asked her to carry a message to Tholindis, a Khaenri'ahn Moon Marrow researcher whose soul lingered there; moved to tears, Tholindis regretted not doing more to help him and shared what she knew of the reflection. Columbina told Rerir that Dainsleif still regarded him as a friend, and Rerir asked her not to die. She also learned it was her own future self who had shielded Hiisi Island from Rerir's kuuvahki bombardment.

9.content:
Moon-Prayer Night is Nod-Krai's biggest festival, when kuuvahki peaks. Columbina planned to return to the moon that night, since she would cease to exist if she stayed. After she was named, Nasha Town turned the festival into a homecoming: "Welcome home, Moon Goddess." For the first time she enjoyed it freely. She tried candy flavours, played games with townsfolk and Fatui alike, fought a balloon war with Arlecchino and Nefer, and tested Nicole's game. She took an Alice-style "Dodoco adventure", shared a gruff goodbye with Sandrone, and had her future read by Barbeloth. She admitted to the Traveler she feared losing what she had just found. Her friends gave her a handmade greeting card, and she hung a wish that all beneath the moon find belonging. Dottore's ambush ended the night.

She now marks her birthday by sensing the moon, since the festival date moves. She imagines a birthday as everyone dancing while people make offerings, and was surprised to learn ordinary birthdays mean cake and friends. The Traveler later returned the greeting card she left behind.

10.comment: Columbina: The Frost Moon and the Traveler's spaceship
10.content:
When she was reborn, the Frost Moon passed through the false sky and stayed within Teyvat. She built a moonlit pathway between the two and travels it at will. She took the Traveler to the moon and revealed their spaceship had been hidden there by the Heavenly Principles, perhaps because something aboard was incompatible with Teyvat or must not be known. She encouraged them to go in, as she had found the courage to step through a door on Moon-Prayer Night. On the moon she described blue kuuvahki like an endless ocean, jellyfish, pink frostfin whales and enormous kuuhenki, and said she counts both the moon and Teyvat as home.

There she told the Traveler she had once thought home was a transaction, and that they had taught her otherwise. She returned her kuuvahki to Nod-Krai, lifted some of Teyvat's restrictions on the Traveler, and gave them a Moon-Prayer Blossom that will never fade. Asked about Snezhnaya, she described Kresnik's Torches, recommended the Korolevskiy Troupe and likened the Tsaritsa to thick ice on a frozen lake. She said she does not believe there has to be an ending.

11.comment: Columbina: Fatui Harbingers in her eyes
11.content: Her voice-overs size up her old colleagues. Pierro, the Jester, is the opposite of his codename: stern, speaking in riddles behind a mask that mocks the world, yet he never smiles. Capitano is respected and feared in equal measure, because creatures used to darkness avoid the light that lengthens their shadows. Pantalone, Regrator, puts a price on everyone; she pictures him congratulating her on her "appreciated value" and finds his empire of wealth boring. Pulcinella, the Rooster, she can imitate perfectly with "money", "that darn Pantalone" and "mark my words"; the two get along in public but scheme against each other. Tartaglia, she hears, camps and barbecues with his family, and that sounds nice to her. She sat in a corner at meetings, mostly asleep.

12.content: Rosalyne taught Columbina always to express gratitude, which is why she thanks the Traveler with the Moon Goddess's Favor. Before the Traveler's journey began, Columbina, Arlecchino and Signora held a tea party in Sandrone's bedroom to comfort her over Alain Guillotin. A tea-party remark by Sandrone to Signora mocks Columbina's lack of social graces. Columbina attended Signora's funeral (shown in a 2022 teaser). She remembers Signora as someone who gave her whole self to love, hate or a dance, "and left others to sing her dirge". She thinks Rosalyne chose her own ending rather than survive in the cocoon.

13.content: Flins thanked her for his rescue and later named her "spirit animal" a free-spirited kuuhenki. Nefer found the kuuvahki message she left on the Traveler's wall, risked blindness viewing her past through Luonnotar (Lauma believed Columbina took the cost on herself), and once sharply scolded her for nearly falling for a Nasha Town scam. Jahoda owes her a shove out of Rerir's line of fire. Illuga politely escorted her out of a restricted area of Piramida. Aino was terrified to learn that the lyre that kept mysteriously appearing for repair was Columbina's; Ineffa recognised her from the Statues of the New Moon. Varka rescued her party from the Wild Hunt and rallied everyone after Dottore's ambush.

14.content: When Columbina began to fade, Alice explained that the world was rejecting her for lack of a foundation. Nicole found the Hyperborean route to the moon and saw that a name could be given in the present. Columbina later learned Nicole has lived since the Moon Sisters' era and called their friendship a continuation of the old bond between Moon Goddesses and angels. She asked Nicole for books to read to the kuuhenki; Nicole sent many with notes, then stopped answering. Columbina hopes she went off to write a book of her own. In 6.3 Nicole, with Alice's backing, joined Varka's plan to stall Dottore, and pulled the Frost Moon down with Varka and Arlecchino. On Moon-Prayer Night Barbeloth's tarot showed her loneliness, new bonds and a transformation; from the Moon's Reflection Columbina found she could tug the "Death" card into that very reading.

15.comment: Columbina: Sunny Summer Fontinalia and "A Homecoming"
15.content: In 6.7 Nefer told her about the Fontinalia Film Festival, and Columbina went to Fontaine, Sandrone's homeland, hoping to find her. Director Xavier cast her as lead actress in the film "A Homecoming", shot partly at the Wingalet, where she learned a Fontainian greeting. The crew argued over whether the heroine should reunite with her old friend; Columbina wanted it but disliked an actor standing in. Sandrone's real return gave the film its happy ending; it then lost the Furina Award to "Great Detective Hurlock". She met Neuvillette and decided he was nothing like Nibelung. The quest launched alongside the limited 6.7 event but remains available as a Story Quest.

16.comment: Columbina: Moon Gazing and Home-Returning Night
16.content: In the Moon Gazing quests (6.7) Columbina met Ninnin on the Frost Moon and helped the Traveler uncover Project Moongazer. She shielded the Moongazers' message as it passed through the false sky, pushing her strength to its limit. She wondered aloud whether anyone among the stars would receive it, and whether they too would want to wave and say "Hello, friend". Afterward she waited at the Traveler's Crater. She promised that if the Traveler ever returns to their birthplace, she will help them as they helped her clean the moon, and suggested they call the celebration "Home-Returning Night".

17.content: The Tsaritsa gave her a "second home" but, Columbina concluded, wanted only the Moon Goddess's power. The first time Columbina sang in the gardens of Zapolyarny Palace, the Tsaritsa stopped and stood listening, expressionless as a statue, as if about to speak, but never did. Columbina thinks she seals her feelings under thick ice and that the world sees only "the Tsaritsa"; perhaps her answers lie buried in snow as Columbina's lay on the moon. She doubts even Snezhnayans know what power their god wields, or that the Tsaritsa accepts it herself. The Tsaritsa issued the Palestar Edict against her and revoked it once Dottore's intentions came to light.

18.content: When the Traveler prepared to leave Nod-Krai for Snezhnaya, Luonnotar told Columbina, and she arranged a farewell party for them at the Flagship. She relayed a message from Sandrone, already in Snezhnograd: not to cause trouble for her there. Columbina did not go to Snezhnaya herself and takes no part in the 7.0-7.1 events there.
